statement: This repo's own main is guarded by TWO CI workflows that both push-trigger on main today: .github/workflows/ci.yml ('Rust CI', job id 'rust-ci', matrixed over ubuntu-latest/windows-latest/macos-latest -- fmt/clippy/test/deny/audit) and .github/workflows/ocentra-enforcer.yml ('Ocentra Enforcer', job id 'ocentra-enforcer', NO matrix -- the self-scan/dogfood gate). The legacy docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md named only the second workflow, used a stale pre-rename job body, AND wrongly assumed a parenthesized-matrix suffix on a job that has never had a matrix. Any future branch-protection desired-state must resolve required contexts from BOTH workflow files, or it silently under-protects main by only gating one of the two CI surfaces.
why: x04's branch_protection.rs verifier fails closed on ANY missing required context -- if a future edit to DesiredProtection::baseline only lists one of the two workflows (e.g. copies the x04 unit-test fixture literally instead of re-deriving from both YAML files), main would be 'protected' by the verifier's own standard but only half-covered in the real GitHub setting, defeating the point.
howToApply: Before changing the required-jobs list in crates/enforcer-install/src/ci/branch_protection.rs's DesiredProtection::baseline call site (or in tests/branch_protection_fixtures.rs's desired()), re-read both .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/ocentra-enforcer.yml's current name:/job-id/strategy.matrix, and update .github/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md's 'Today's resolved required contexts' section in the same change. Do not add a third workflow's job without doing the same three-way update (module fixture list, integration-test desired(), doc).

evidence.ref: .github/workflows/ci.yml (name: Rust CI, jobs.rust-ci, matrix.os); .github/workflows/ocentra-enforcer.yml (name: Ocentra Enforcer, jobs.ocentra-enforcer, no strategy block); docs/BRANCH_PROTECTION.md (legacy, superseded)

statement: On this Windows machine, cargo test -p enforcer-install (and any crate whose compiled test binary name contains the substring 'install') fails with `error 740: The requested operation requires elevation` when invoking the test executable directly, even though no build.rs or embedded manifest requests elevation anywhere in the crate. Setting __COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker before the cargo test invocation resolves it immediately -- Windows' installer-detection app-compat heuristic is triggering purely off the binary's file name, not any actual manifest bit. Reconfirmed here for a second, independently-compiled test binary (tests/branch_protection_fixtures.rs's own .exe), in addition to the crate's --lib binary already documented by c05 (proof/install/c05-sessionstart.txt).
why: Any worker touching enforcer-install's test suite on Windows will hit this and may misdiagnose it as a real bug in their own code (it looks like a process/permissions error, not a lint or logic failure) if they don't know the __COMPAT_LAYER workaround already exists and is environment-only.
howToApply: Always prefix cargo test -p enforcer-install (any target: --lib, --test <name>, or bare) with __COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker on Windows. This applies per-test-binary, not per-crate -- a NEW integration test file gets its own .exe and will need the same env var, confirmed by this workpack's own tests/branch_protection_fixtures.rs hitting it independently of the --lib binary.

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-install --lib branch_protection (error 740) vs same command with __COMPAT_LAYER=RunAsInvoker set (11/11 pass); repeated for --test branch_protection_fixtures (7/7 pass)
